A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same particle-based inference-time scaling research. Their text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original MATH500 and AIME 2024 experiments, scaling curves, and ablations of reward models, aggregation, temperature and computation allocation.

after.justification: V4 retains original mathematical-reasoning experiments and reports additional FinanceBench, NumGLUE Chemistry and generator-model results.

M1.justification: The generation, reward scoring, softmax resampling, Particle Gibbs and parallel-tempering procedures are retained, as are the four aggregation strategies. V4 newly specifies default aggregation and final-answer selection, but does not establish that these disclosures reflect a procedural change.

E1.justification: Beyond the retained MATH500 and AIME tasks, v4 evaluates FinanceBench's document-grounded financial question answering and NumGLUE Task 2's chemistry-related numerical reasoning. These substantially broaden the evaluated domains and task requirements.

E2.justification: V1 explicitly excludes standalone beam search; v4 adds evaluated beam-search and self-consistency comparisons in Table 1. Section 5 also adds a comparison against reported TSMC results. The relocated Llama table retains only greedy/PF rows, although WBoN and DVTS remain in the scaling plots.

E3.justification: Table 1's stated generation budget changes from 64 to 32; v4 Appendix F retains 64-generation evaluations. New protocols use 8 particles for FinanceBench and 32 for NumGLUE. Additional evaluated generator configurations include general Qwen, phi-4, Mistral-Small and DeepSeekMath. The PDFs do not establish which existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V4 Figure 1 adds a concrete scored example showing how an initially disfavored trajectory ultimately produces the correct answer. The existing reward-model, aggregation, temperature, Particle Gibbs and parallel-tempering ablations are retained in Figure 5 and Appendix B.

E5.justification: V4's checklist newly reports that some experiments were repeated during development and explains why experiments were not uniformly repeated to produce error bars. It supplies no exact run counts, seeds or quantitative uncertainty estimates and does not establish an increase in runs.

E6.justification: V4 replaces and adds substantial results. Qwen2.5-Math-7B PF changes from 87.0% MATH500 and 23.3% AIME at 64 generations to 87.7% and 10/30 at 32 generations; these are different-setting results. New Table 2 reports PF accuracies of 70.33% on FinanceBench and 84.22% on NumGLUE, with additional model results in Appendix F.

T1.justification: V1 contains the probabilistic formulation but no corresponding theorem. V4 introduces an unbiasedness theorem for expected accuracy in Section 3.1 and a proof in Appendix C, alongside broader assertions about unbiased posterior expectations. This adds substantive formal claims to the retained mathematical framework.

C1.justification: V4 shifts the central motivating failure from reward hacking to premature pruning and expands its headline empirical claims to reasoning beyond mathematics. Its abstract extends the 4–16x scaling claim to general reasoning tasks, while retaining the core particle-filtering contribution and small-model scaling claims.

C2.justification: V4 develops early pruning as a concrete failure mechanism and newly hypothesizes that mathematical PRMs learn transferable reasoning-evaluation capabilities. The existing limitations concerning reward-model latency, output formatting and domain-dependent tuning largely remain.

D1.justification: V1 provides a project link and states that code is available; v4 removes that access information and explicitly defers code release until acceptance in checklist item 5. V4 also newly specifies default product aggregation and ORM-based final-answer selection, while retaining the prompt templates and mathematical answer-scoring procedure.

R1.justification: V4 substantially expands positioning against previous SMC approaches for language models, including token-based steering and twisted SMC. Section 5 distinguishes the proposed approach through its claimed training-free and verifier-free operation, adds a TSMC comparison, and introduces connections to Boltzmann exploration and bandits.

P1.justification: The introduction and method exposition are extensively rewritten, and the title gains 'Rollout Roulette.' Related work moves after evaluation; aggregation details, algorithm descriptions and computation-allocation discussions are reorganized into separately named appendices.

P2.justification: V4 changes the main text from two columns to one, adds scored reasoning illustrations, relocates existing schematics, and combines three ablation plots into Figure 5. It also restructures the main comparison table and adds separate non-math and additional-generator tables.

improvement.justification: New domain evaluations, direct beam-search/self-consistency comparisons and closer engagement with prior SMC research strengthen the empirical case and positioning. However, v4 extends the 4–16x claim beyond mathematics without corresponding scaling curves, adds an unbiasedness guarantee not established for Algorithm 1 by Appendix C, and changes stated code access from available to deferred. These substantive gains and validity/reproducibility concerns leave the net quality direction uncertain.
